open_findings.title: PDF_INTERNAL_SECRET unset on Supabase project; 23 report edge fns using hardcoded fallback
open_findings.evidence: secrets-canary probe: PDF_INTERNAL_SECRET.set=false; get-start-score-report v35 source contains `Deno.env.get('PDF_INTERNAL_SECRET')??'st-pdf-internal-2026'`
open_findings.impact: Any attacker who reads deployed edge fn source can forge x-internal-token: st-pdf-internal-2026 + arbitrary x-user-email to receive fully rendered reports (KYC/AML, financials, ownership, HR audit, I-9, etc.) for any org.
open_findings.remediation: 1) Enumerate all Vercel callers of the 23 fns (grep PDF_INTERNAL_SECRET across repos - completed). 2) Generate strong random secret. 3) Set PDF_INTERNAL_SECRET on Supabase edge fn secrets. 4) Simultaneously set on all Vercel callers. 5) Deploy edge fns v-next with hardcoded fallback removed (fail-closed). 6) Verify canary shows all values properly set.
open_findings.vercel_callers_grep_status: REM-008 identifies these; overlap analysis needed

open_findings.title: lender + Brokers pinned to Next.js 14.2.5 (below CVE-2025-29927 fix)
open_findings.evidence: package.json dependencies.next = '14.2.5' in both lender (banking-treasury-portal) and Brokers repos. Fix was Next.js 14.2.25.
open_findings.impact: Middleware bypass — attackers can craft requests that skip middleware auth checks and reach protected routes directly.
open_findings.remediation: Bump both repos to ^14.2.25 or higher (Client-Dashboard on 14.2.35, Client-EP on 14.2.35 are the current fleet standard). Deploy, verify. Add CI gate.

open_findings.title: Hardcoded JWT fallback secrets in 12 apps
open_findings.evidence: grep across all repo middleware.js/next.config.js/login-route/lib-auth files identified `process.env.X || 'literal-string'` pattern in 12 repos with actual secret values.
open_findings.impact: If ANY app's JWT env var is unset (rotation window, config drift, accidental deletion, new deploy), the app falls back to a source-visible string, making JWT signing forgeable by anyone with access to the deployed code.
open_findings.remediation: For each of the 12 apps: 1) Confirm the env var is set on Vercel. 2) Replace `process.env.X || 'literal'` with fail-closed `getSecret()` throw pattern (chamber Phase 0.5 blueprint). 3) Deploy. 4) After all 12 shipped, do fleet-wide gitleaks scan to confirm no residuals.

open_findings.title: Unauthenticated INSERT policies on 5 production tables
open_findings.evidence: pg_policies query: 5 policies with qual=true, cmd=INSERT, roles={public}
open_findings.impact: Unauthenticated requests can create rows. Document_View_Log likely intentional (analytics), but Document_Shares and Compliance_Item_Documents allowing unauthenticated INSERT is a data-integrity risk.
open_findings.remediation: For each: audit the current caller pattern, replace qual=true with a real access check (org membership + entity access), or move the INSERT to a SECURITY DEFINER RPC with server-side authorization.

open_findings.title: 155 tables have RLS on but zero policies (deny-all effectively; audit-visible)
open_findings.impact: SOC 2 finding: RLS declared but policies never authored. Functionally these tables are locked (deny-all), but they signal incomplete authorization design. If a policy is added later that isn't tight, exposure emerges.
open_findings.remediation: For each table, either (a) confirm service-role-only access is the design intent and document that decision, or (b) author appropriate policies for authenticated roles. Batch by domain: Investment_*, Pro_*, cap_*, stripe_*.

open_findings.title: 47 authenticated-role tables with qual=true policies (any authenticated JWT can read)
open_findings.impact: Any authenticated user across any portal can read financially/regulatorily sensitive data. Some are legitimate reference data (dol_form5500, etc.); the financial holdings tables are not.
open_findings.remediation: Split the list into (a) legitimate authenticated-read reference data (leave as-is, mark policy names with _public_lookup_intentional suffix), and (b) sensitive holdings that need org-scoped policies. Michael to approve the split.

open_findings.title: @start-today/platform-auth keystone package not yet built
open_findings.impact: Every future portal reimplements auth from scratch, replicating this class of bugs (fallback secrets, MFA gate ordering, cookie handling).
open_findings.remediation: Build shared package with: fail-closed secret loader, jose session verify+sign, org-binding helper, MFA gate middleware factory, cookie handling. Migrate portals incrementally starting with newest (chamber pattern is the reference).

open_findings.title: MFA still password-only on finance, property, plan, work, mga, mylegal, marketplace
open_findings.evidence: auth matrix shows MFA mode 'A?' or '?' for these repos - either not enforced or partially implemented. mga has no MFA marker at all.
open_findings.impact: Provider-side and internal-tools portals accept password-only login. Session hijack via credential leak becomes portal-wide compromise.
open_findings.remediation: Apply chamber Phase 0.5 blueprint to each: fail-closed getSecret + pending-token cookie + login-then-TOTP flow. Order by user count and blast radius: work (internal escalation, most privileged), finance (financial data), property, plan, mga, mylegal, marketplace.

open_findings.title: mga login untested for session-before-MFA pattern
open_findings.evidence: mga middleware sets MGA_JWT_SECRET with fallback but shows no MFA marker; login route not detected at any expected path.
open_findings.impact: Same class of vulnerability as chamber pre-Phase 0.5: if login mints a full session before TOTP validation, MFA can be bypassed.
open_findings.remediation: Locate mga login route (probably under app/api/auth/login/route.js — needs manual read since B2b probes didn't find it). Audit for setSession/issueSession calls occurring before TOTP verify. Apply fix if present.

open_findings.title: 1128 SECURITY DEFINER functions callable by anon/authenticated (attack surface)
open_findings.evidence: 574 fns callable by authenticated, 554 by anon. Each is a potential unauthorized escalation vector.
open_findings.remediation: Triage: identify fns intentionally exposed (RPCs called from client), revoke execute from anon/authenticated on all others. Combine with search_path fix (REM-013).

open_findings.title: 15 of 25 repos have no security headers in next.config.js
open_findings.impact: Missing HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy. Clickjacking, MIME-sniffing, HTTPS downgrade risks.
open_findings.remediation: Add async headers() to next.config.js in each app. Reference implementation: Client-EP or attorney-dashboard. Include CSP for portals handling sensitive data (client-facing at minimum).

open_findings.title: MFA enrollment 14% platform-wide (7/50 auth.users)
open_findings.impact: SOC 2 CC6.1/CC6.2 finding: MFA infrastructure present but adoption incomplete. Chamber operators 3/11 (27%), other portals unknown enrollment.
open_findings.remediation: For each portal with MFA infrastructure: force enrollment on next login (Mode A). Track enrollment %, target 100% before SOC 2 Type II window opens.

open_findings.title: 226 functions with mutable search_path (Supabase advisor)
open_findings.impact: Search path injection can hijack function calls, redirect to attacker-controlled schemas.
open_findings.remediation: SET search_path TO 'public','extensions' on every SECURITY DEFINER function. Batch via generated ALTER FUNCTION statements. Add CI gate to prevent new SECURITY DEFINER fns without search_path.

open_findings.title: 7 public SELECT + 4 anon SELECT policies (unauthenticated readable tables)
open_findings.remediation: Most look like reference/configuration data intentionally readable. Confirm each with the domain owner, add `_public_lookup_intentional` suffix to policy name to document intent, or restrict if data has changed sensitivity.

open_findings.title: 82 SECURITY DEFINER views
open_findings.impact: SECURITY DEFINER views bypass RLS of caller. Legitimate use cases exist (aggregations, admin dashboards) but each should be reviewed.
open_findings.remediation: Enumerate and classify each view. Convert to plain views where possible; document remaining as intentional.

open_findings.title: Real auth on get-*-report edge fn routes (client-side)
open_findings.notes: The Vercel-side wrapper routes for report generation should not blindly pass user email as x-user-email header. They should verify the session first, then set the header from the verified session.
open_findings.remediation: Blocked pending REM-001 rotation.

open_findings.title: Parameterized data layer / eq.${} injection surface
open_findings.impact: PostgREST query construction using string interpolation is vulnerable to filter injection.
open_findings.remediation: Replace with parameterized query builders. Prior counts: Work 86, mylegal 52, attorney 33 instances. Need fresh sweep post-remediation.

open_findings.title: Only 4 of 25 repos have Content-Security-Policy defined
open_findings.remediation: Add CSP to all client-facing portals. Start with report-only mode to catch violations, then move to enforce.

open_findings.title: sales portal has no middleware.js
open_findings.impact: Sales relies entirely on route-level auth guards. If any route omits the guard, it's exposed. No middleware layer as defense in depth.
open_findings.remediation: Add sales middleware.js following Client-Dashboard pattern.

open_findings.title: AUDIT_PROXY_SECRET stray in DEMO Supabase project
open_findings.evidence: Set on tbihmlnqpwdeiethgwaf during initial mistake; PROD project now has correct value. DEMO has no gh-* fns so the value is inert.

open_findings.title: readiness-reports storage bucket is public
open_findings.impact: If bucket contains generated reports with real org data, they're accessible without auth.
open_findings.remediation: Audit bucket contents. If PII-bearing PDFs present, make bucket private and issue signed URLs for access.

open_findings.title: AUDIT_PROXY_SECRET rotation needed post-audit
open_findings.evidence: Value was passed as header in tool call during this session; will be in transcript.
open_findings.remediation: After audit complete: rotate AUDIT_PROXY_SECRET to a fresh value, update AUDIT_PROXY_SECRET on Supabase. Alternatively, delete the gh-* proxies now that the audit is done.

closed_findings.title: gh-read, gh-read-repo, gh-search proxies unauthenticated GitHub PAT exposure
closed_findings.verification: Unauth calls → 401; authenticated calls with x-audit-token → 200. Canary probe: AUDIT_PROXY_SECRET.set=true, chars=64.
closed_findings.notes: Closed during this audit run — pattern demonstrates the state-file lifecycle.
